From your window to your notch

An illustrative walkthrough. Press left Shift and right Shift together to capture an app; the aperture in the notch closes like a shutter. The window becomes a card, and its accessibility tree comes with it. The card flies into the notch shelf, ready to copy. With history on, you can search every shot later.

Press ⇧ ⇧

Both Shift keys at once. The aperture in your notch closes like a shutter.

The context comes, too.

Not just pixels: the text and every control, straight from the window’s accessibility tree.

Into the notch.

Your shot lands on a tiny shelf, one hover away from your next conversation.

And back again.

Turn on history to search every shot you’ve taken. It never leaves your Mac.

Free & open source · Apple silicon · macOS 15+

A little heads-up. NotchShot is signed but not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS may block the first launch. Allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security, and from then on it updates itself. Capture needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions, and what’s captured and pasted can vary by app.
